results.summary_before: This is an analog comparator built by the MNEL team from USFQ that compares two voltages or currents and outputs a binary signal indicating which input is greater. It is tested by applying known input voltages and verifying that the output transitions at the expected threshold across the full input range. No external hardware is required beyond the analog input, reference, and output pins. A silicon test report notes the design was broken because the supply voltage appeared higher than the 1.8V rating of the transistors.

results.summary_before: This is a 4-bit R2R digital-to-analog converter with an integrated sawtooth waveform generator, implemented in analog. It can be driven externally by setting the external data pin high and applying 4 input bits, or it can generate a sawtooth internally when external data is low, with frequency set by loading a divider. Testing requires a multimeter on the analog output pin to observe the voltage or sawtooth waveform. A silicon test report confirms it worked at a 10 kHz clock, producing the expected sawtooth wave.

results.summary_before: This TL-Verilog project implements the Mastermind game, where the user guesses a hidden four-color combination using eight color inputs and receives feedback on correct colors and positions via eight LEDs. A random answer is chosen by pressing a button, guesses are made with four button presses, and the game indicates a win or loss after ten rounds. External hardware includes two Pmod BTN modules for eight push buttons, a Pmod8LD for eight LEDs, and a splitter cable. The design is a complete interactive game with clear testing instructions.

results.summary_before: This analog project generates two sinusoidal oscillators centered around 0.9V, targeting 20MHz and 21MHz. The oscillators are based on ring oscillators and should oscillate regardless of chip corner, though frequency varies. Silicon testing showed they run slower than intended (approx 13 and 14.2MHz) with waveforms between sinusoidal and triangular. No external hardware is required for operation.
